description: A pattern such as `/products/{sku}` whose named segments become route values that bind to handler parameters with the same name.
A suffix such as `{id:int}` that decides whether a route matches; a failed constraint means no match and a 404, so it is not a validation tool.
The single place a parameter is read from (route, query, header, body, form or DI), chosen by an explicit `[From*]` attribute or by the inference rules.
An attribute that binds each property of a record or struct as if it were a separate handler parameter, without recursive model binding.
The .NET 10 registration that makes minimal APIs validate DataAnnotations on query, header and body values and return 400 before the handler runs.
An interface whose `Validate` method holds cross-field rules and runs only after every property attribute has passed.
A `RouteHandlerOptions` setting, `true` only in Development by default, that turns binding failures into `BadHttpRequestException` instead of a bare 400.
